title: Japanese conditionals: と
summary: と after a clause means "when this happens, that and only that follows". It is the same exclusive と as in "A and B", and it grows into "I must".

blocks.text: Japanese has several "if / when" tools. This lesson starts with the oldest and simplest: **と**.
The same と you already know

Japanese has two "and" particles for nouns. **や** is open: it lists examples and maybe more. **と** is **exclusive**: exactly those two. The conditional と is this same particle, now sitting after a whole clause. (The quoting と, as in 「行くと言った」, is a different word.)

Why can と follow a clause at all? Logical particles such as や normally attach only to nouns, but と is not a logical particle: it can also sit after a whole clause, and that is how it works as "if / when".
Because と is exclusive, "A と B" says that when A is the case, **only B** follows. It suits natural laws, habits, and things that always go together.
冬になると寒くなる。 When winter comes, it gets cold.

blocks.en: When winter comes, it gets cold.

blocks.jp: このボタンを押すとドアが開く。
blocks.en: When you press this button, the door opens.

blocks.text: Speakers use the absolute feel for warnings: they present a likely result as if it were certain.

blocks.jp: 食べ過ぎると病気になるよ。
blocks.en: If you overeat, you will get sick.

blocks.jp: ゲームばかりしていると、試験に落ちるよ。
blocks.en: If you keep playing games, you will fail the exam.

blocks.text: A negative clause plus と, with a negative result left understood, becomes necessity. The result is often just ダメ ("no good") or いけない ("it won't do"), or nothing at all.

blocks.jp: もう行かないとダメだ。
blocks.en: I really have to go now.

blocks.jp: 毎日勉強しないといけない。
blocks.en: I have to study every day.

items: **Clause + と**: when / if this, then (only) that.
Same と as in "A と B" (and nothing else).
**Negative + と (+ ダメ / いけない)**: I must.

questions.instruction: Why is と natural in this sentence?
options: A natural law: one inevitable result
questions.note: と: when A, only B follows.

questions.prompt: このスイッチを押す＿＿、電気がつく。
questions.en: When you press this switch, the light comes on.

questions.prompt: 左に曲がる＿＿、駅が見えます。
questions.note: と: one thing follows the other.
questions.en: If you turn left, you will see the station.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "I have to study now"?

questions.prompt: 電車が来るから、急がないとダメだよ。
questions.en: A train is coming, so you have to hurry.

questions.prompt: 薬を飲まないと、治らないよ。
options: Without medicine, you will not get better
questions.note: と states an almost certain result.
questions.en: If you don't take medicine, you won't get better.

questions.instruction: In which sentence is と the quotation と?
options: 先生は明日休むと言った。
ボタンを押すと音が出る。

questions.prompt: や lists things openly, while と lists exactly those things.
questions.note: や is open; と is exclusive.

questions.instruction: What is left unsaid after 〜ないと at the end of a sentence?
options: A bad result, like ダメ
questions.note: If I don't, it is bad.

questions.prompt: 早く行かないと、遅れるよ！
questions.note: Negative と: if not, then the bad result.
questions.en: If you don't go soon, you'll be late!

options: 秋になると、涼しくなる。
窓を開けると、風が入る。
秋になるを、涼しくなる。
毎日歩くと、元気になる。
questions.note: A condition needs と, not を.

questions.instruction: Which sentence gives a warning with と?
options: 夜ふかしすると、あした眠くなるよ。
夜ふかしをしてください。
questions.note: と presents a likely result as certain.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "I have to study"?
options: 勉強しないといけない。
questions.note: Negative + と + いけない: must.

questions.prompt: If you push the door, it opens.
questions.en: If you push the door, it opens.

questions.prompt: If you don't leave soon, you will be late.
questions.en: If you don't leave soon, you will be late.

questions.prompt: When I drink coffee, I cannot sleep.
questions.en: When I drink coffee, I cannot sleep.

questions.prompt: If you add sugar, it gets sweet.
questions.en: If you add sugar, it gets sweet.

questions.prompt: I have to go home now.
questions.en: I have to go home now.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that means "if I don't"
questions.en: I have to get up early tomorrow.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that says "when this happens"
questions.en: When you press the button, the light comes on.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that is the quotation と
questions.en: Dad said he will be back soon.

questions.prompt: 夜ふかしばかりしていると、病気になるよ。
questions.note: と presents a likely result as if it were certain.
questions.en: If you keep staying up late, you will get sick.
